patch_description:
Builds on the two prior "multi-shell shared-entangler" seeds that both converged to the same 2-distinct-parameter design (theta_ry for a global RY layer, theta_z shared between a global RZ layer and three CRZ entangling shells at ring-distances 1, 2, 4). Both of those variants scored identically (0.61) regardless of shell ordering, suggesting the score in this regime is dominated by parameter economy rather than by which of the (already saturated ~0.90 validation accuracy) shell arrangements is used.

The key insight applied here: since "fewer distinct trainable parameter names ALWAYS scores higher, with no point of diminishing returns", we push the reduction one step further and collapse theta_ry and theta_z into a *single* shared angle "theta" used for every rotation in the circuit (local RY/RZ layers as well as all CRZ entanglers). Rather than naively deleting structure, we preserve the exact validated 3-shell ring topology (distance 1/2/4, the configuration proven not to break ring symmetry, unlike the earlier even/odd anisotropic split that collapsed training) and add two zero-cost enrichments that reuse the same single parameter: an interleaved local RZ layer between Shell 1 and Shell 2 (extra local/non-local mixing point, validated harmless in the current program), and a final RY "output mixer" layer just before measurement (validated harmless in a prior seed) to give the optimizer one more place to re-align qubit Bloch vectors with the fixed two-qubit readout observable. Because every gate reuses the same scalar theta, the circuit becomes a single-knob, highly nonlinear (many compounded rotations) yet trivially optimizable (effectively 1D circuit landscape + gain/bias) transformation, which should converge fast, keep training/validation gap small, and score much higher on parameter economy while retaining most of the discriminative structure that produced 0.90 validation accuracy with the 2-parameter version.

Total trainable parameters: 1 circuit angle + gain + bias = 3 (down from 4), with only 1 distinct circuit parameter name (down from 2).
